column1: # Mirrors for sources whose upstream host is the only one serving them, for tools/fetch-sources.sh
# and tools/verify-signatures.sh. A mirror serves upstream's own file, so the lock's hash decides
# what is built wherever the bytes came from, and a signature from a mirror must still verify. A
# distribution keeps a version only while a release carries it: a mirror behind the pin answers 404,
# and the next one is asked. fetch-sources.sh tries them after the source's own host and before
# Gentoo's distfiles; verify-signatures.sh only when upstream's own signature cannot be fetched.
#   package    the source name, as in tools/fetch-sources.sh
#   url        the file at the mirror, {VER} standing for the manifest's version
#   signature  the suffix of upstream's own signature kept beside it there, or - for none
# Each row was checked when added: the mirror's file has the lock's hash, and its signature was
# made by the key upstream's own is made by. CI holds every row's file to the lock again each week
# (fetch-sources.sh --check-mirrors), and a dispatch of CI checks a new row on its branch.
# Void names its package after the series, so the row moves with a series change.
# kernel.org keeps each series in a directory of its own, so the row moves with a series change.
